HTML section("venue-dubletten", 130, "08c · Venue-Dubletten", "Venue-Dubletten", "Aliasnamen werden auf eine kanonische Venue gemappt.", [ "Venue-Dubletten", "Venue Alias", "kanonische Venue", "Autocomplete", "LLM Venue-Fallback" ], [ link("Venue-Dubletten", "/backend/settings/edit?section=venue_duplicate_mappings"), link("Locations", "/backend/venues") ], <<~HTML),

  • Öffentliche Eventkarten und Detailseiten nutzen kanonische Venue-Stammdaten.
  • Nach Mapping-Änderungen kann ein Backfill Verknüpfungen aktualisieren.
HTML section("queue-importer", 140, "09 · Queue", "Queue, Importer & Importer-Konfiguration", "Raw-Importer, Merge, LLM-Enrichment, Scheduler und Run-Status.", [ "Queue", "Importer", "Importer-Konfiguration", "RawEventImport", "ImportRun", "Solid Queue", "Merge", "Scheduler" ], [ link("Queue", "/backend/import_sources"), link("Raw Importer", "/backend/import_sources?section=raw_importer"), link("Merge Importer", "/backend/import_sources?section=merge_importer"), link("LLM-Enrichment", "/backend/import_sources?section=llm_enrichment") ], <<~HTML),

Die Queue zeigt automatische und manuell gestartete Jobs. Ein Run ist ein Protokoll, kein Inhalt selbst: Inhalte liegen danach als RawEventImport, Event, EventOffer, Eventbild, LLM-Datensatz oder Social-Draft vor.

Raw Importerholt Anbieterfeeds und schreibt RawEventImport.
Merge Importererstellt oder aktualisiert Events, Offers, Bilder, Venue- und Reihen-Zuordnung.
LLM-Enrichmentergänzt Genres, Sub-Genres, Links und Texte.
HTML section("llm-enrichment", 150, "10 · LLM", "LLM-Enrichment", "OpenAI, Websuche, strukturierte Antworten, Cache-Hits und Venue-Fallbacks.", [ "LLM-Enrichment", "OpenAI", "Structured Outputs", "Responses API", "SerpApi", "OpenWebNinja", "Cache-Hits", "Venue-Fallbacks", "Run-Protokolle" ], [ link("LLM-Queue", "/backend/import_sources?section=llm_enrichment"), link("LLM-Settings", "/backend/settings/edit?section=llm_enrichment") ], <<~HTML),

LLM-Enrichment arbeitet auf vorhandenen Events. Es schreibt Genres, Sub-Genres, Beschreibungen, Links und belastbare Venue-Fallbacks zurück, erzeugt aber keine neuen Events.

  • Genres kommen aus der festen Liste, Sub-Genres sind fachlich frei.
  • Homepage-, Instagram-, Facebook- und YouTube-Links dürfen nur aus Kandidaten gewählt werden.
  • Cache-Hits bei Websuche werden im Run-Protokoll sichtbar dokumentiert.
HTML section("meta-publishing", 160, "11 · Meta", "Meta Publishing", "Instagram/Facebook-Verbindungen, Social-Drafts, Publish-Fehler und Token-Health.", [ "Meta Publishing", "Instagram", "Facebook", "Social-Drafts", "Publish-Fehler", "Token-Health" ], [ link("Meta Publishing Settings", "/backend/settings/edit?section=meta_connection"), link("Meta-Verbindung", "/backend/meta_connection"), link("Event-Social-Tab", "/backend/events") ], <<~HTML),

Meta Publishing verbindet das Backend getrennt mit Instagram und Facebook. Events können Social-Drafts bekommen, die geprüft und veröffentlicht werden.

VerbindungOAuth-Zugriff auf Meta-Seite, Instagram Business Account oder Facebook Page.
Publish AttemptProtokoll eines Veröffentlichungsversuchs mit Erfolg oder Fehler.
Token-HealthStatusprüfung, Ablaufwarnung und Refresh-Versuch.
HTML section("frontend-suche", 170, "12 · Frontend", "Frontend-Suche", "Wie die öffentliche Suchbox Begriffe, Zeiträume, Venues und SKS-Kontext behandelt.", [ "Suchbox", "Frontend", "Suche", "Venue", "Zeitphrasen", "SKS-Filter" ], [ link("Öffentliche Suche", "/search"), link("Eventliste", "/events") ], <<~HTML),

Die Suchbox kann freie Begriffe, Monats- und Wochenendphrasen sowie Venue-Fragmente erkennen. Ohne Suchbegriff startet die Browse-Logik oft im SKS-/Highlight-Kontext; mit Suchbegriff wird breiter über öffentliche Events gesucht.

  • Nur live veröffentlichte und zeitlich sichtbare Events erscheinen öffentlich.
  • Interne Redaktionsnotizen, Social-Drafts und viele Rohimportfelder sind nicht Teil der öffentlichen Suche.
HTML section("consent-banner", 180, "12a · Consent", "Consent-Banner", "Warum externe Medien und Tracking nicht für alle Besucher gleich aussehen.", [ "Consent-Banner", "YouTube", "Analytics", "Meta Pixel", "externe Medien", "Frontend" ], [ link("Startseite", "/"), link("News", "/news"), link("Datenschutz", "/datenschutz") ], <<~HTML),

Der Consent-Banner erscheint auf öffentlichen Seiten, nicht im Backend. Er steuert optionale Statistikdienste und externe Medien wie YouTube.

Keine ZustimmungAnalytics und Meta Pixel bleiben deaktiviert, YouTube bleibt Platzhalter.
Medien erlaubtYouTube-iframe wird geladen; vorher ist das fehlende iframe kein Backend-Fehler.
HTML section("caching-sichtbarkeit", 190, "12b · Caching", "Caching & Sichtbarkeit", "Warum Änderungen manchmal zeitversetzt sichtbar werden.", [ "Caching", "Sichtbarkeit", "Fragment-Cache", "Lazy Loading", "Media Proxy", "Cache-Hit" ], [ link("Startseite", "/"), link("Homepage-Lane Nachladen", "/events/homepage_lane") ], <<~HTML),

Stuttgart-Live nutzt mehrere Cache-Ebenen. Fragment-Caches für Lanes enthalten Events, Venue, kanonische Venue, Dubletten-Setting, Offers und Bilder im Cache-Key. Untere Homepage-Lanes laden erst per JavaScript. Browser- und Media-Cache können Bilder verzögert wirken lassen. LLM-Websuche wird etwa eine Woche gecacht; Cache-Hits bleiben im Run sichtbar.

require "digest"

class BackendHandbookSection < ApplicationRecord
  SLUG_FORMAT = /\A[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\z/

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:position, :id) }

  before_validation :normalize_links

  validates :slug, presence: true, uniqueness: true, format: { with: SLUG_FORMAT }
  validates :position, :title, :body_html, :body_text, :source_digest, presence: true
  validate :links_must_have_label_and_local_path

  class << self
    def sync_defaults!(definitions = BackendHandbookDefaults.definitions)
      normalized_definitions = definitions.each_with_index.map do |definition, index|
        normalized_definition(definition, fallback_position: index + 1)
      end
      slugs = normalized_definitions.map { |definition| definition.fetch(:slug) }
      deleted_slugs = []

      transaction do
        normalized_definitions.each do |attributes|
          section = find_or_initialize_by(slug: attributes.fetch(:slug))
          section.assign_attributes(attributes)
          section.save! if section.changed?
        end

        where.not(slug: slugs).find_each do |section|
          deleted_slugs << section.slug
          section.destroy!
        end
      end

      { synced_count: normalized_definitions.size, deleted_slugs: deleted_slugs }
    end

    def search(query)
      normalized_query = query.to_s.squish
      return ordered if normalized_query.blank?

      tsquery_sql = sanitize_sql_array([ "websearch_to_tsquery('german', ?)", normalized_query ])
      headline_options = "StartSel=<mark>, StopSel=</mark>, MaxFragments=2, MinWords=4, MaxWords=22"

      select(
        "#{quoted_table_name}.*, " \
        "ts_rank_cd(search_vector, #{tsquery_sql}) AS search_rank, " \
        "ts_headline('german', body_text, #{tsquery_sql}, #{connection.quote(headline_options)}) AS search_excerpt"
      )
        .where("search_vector @@ #{tsquery_sql}")
        .order(Arel.sql("search_rank DESC, position ASC, id ASC"))
    end

    def body_text_for(body_html)
      ActionView::Base.full_sanitizer.sanitize(body_html.to_s).squish
    end

    private

    def normalized_definition(definition, fallback_position:)
      body_html = definition.fetch(:body_html).to_s.strip
      attributes = {
        slug: definition.fetch(:slug).to_s,
        parent_slug: definition[:parent_slug].presence,
        position: definition[:position].presence || fallback_position,
        section_label: definition[:section_label].to_s,
        title: definition.fetch(:title).to_s,
        summary: definition[:summary].to_s,
        body_html: body_html,
        body_text: body_text_for(body_html),
        keywords: Array(definition[:keywords]).map { |keyword| keyword.to_s.strip }.reject(&:blank?).uniq,
        links: normalized_links(definition[:links])
      }
      attributes.merge(source_digest: source_digest_for(attributes))
    end

    def normalized_links(links)
      Array(links).map do |link|
        link.to_h.stringify_keys.slice("label", "path", "kind").compact
      end
    end

    def source_digest_for(attributes)
      Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(JSON.generate(attributes.sort.to_h))
    end
  end

  private

  def normalize_links
    self.links = self.class.send(:normalized_links, links)
  end

  def links_must_have_label_and_local_path
    return if links.is_a?(Array) && links.all? { |link| valid_link?(link) }

    errors.add(:links, "müssen je einen Titel und einen lokalen Pfad enthalten")
  end

  def valid_link?(link)
    return false unless link.is_a?(Hash)

    label = link["label"].to_s.strip
    path = link["path"].to_s.strip
    label.present? && path.start_with?("/") && !path.start_with?("//")
  end
end

module Backend::HandbookHelper
  HANDBOOK_ALLOWED_TAGS = %w[
    a br code dd details div dl dt em h2 h3 h4 li mark ol p pre span strong summary table tbody td th thead tr ul
  ].freeze
  HANDBOOK_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES = %w[aria-label class href id rel target].freeze

  def handbook_body(section)
    sanitize(section.body_html, tags: HANDBOOK_ALLOWED_TAGS, attributes: HANDBOOK_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES)
  end

  def handbook_excerpt(section)
    excerpt = section.try(:search_excerpt).presence || truncate(section.body_text, length: 180)
    sanitize(excerpt, tags: %w[mark], attributes: [])
  end
end

module Backend
  class HandbookController < ApplicationController
    before_action :require_handbook_access!

    def show
      @query = params[:q].to_s.strip
      @sections = BackendHandbookSection.ordered.to_a
      @results = handbook_results
      @selected_section = selected_section
    end

    private

    def require_handbook_access!
      return if current_user&.blog_access?

      redirect_to root_path, alert: "Kein Zugriff auf das Backend-Handbuch."
    end

    def handbook_results
      return @sections if @query.blank?

      BackendHandbookSection.search(@query).to_a
    end

    def selected_section
      selected_slug = params[:section].to_s
      if selected_slug.present?
        return @results.find { |section| section.slug == selected_slug } || @sections.find { |section| section.slug == selected_slug }
      end

      @results.first || @sections.first
    end
  end
end

end

-class BackendHandbookSection < ApplicationRecord

+require "digest"
+
+class BackendHandbookSection < ApplicationRecord
+  SLUG_FORMAT = /\A[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\z/
+
+  scope :ordered, -> { order(:position, :id) }
+
+  before_validation :normalize_links
+
+  validates :slug, presence: true, uniqueness: true, format: { with: SLUG_FORMAT }
+  validates :position, :title, :body_html, :body_text, :source_digest, presence: true
+  validate :links_must_have_label_and_local_path
+
+  class << self
+    def sync_defaults!(definitions = BackendHandbookDefaults.definitions)
+      normalized_definitions = definitions.each_with_index.map do |definition, index|
+        normalized_definition(definition, fallback_position: index + 1)
+      end
+      slugs = normalized_definitions.map { |definition| definition.fetch(:slug) }
+      deleted_slugs = []
+
+      transaction do
+        normalized_definitions.each do |attributes|
+          section = find_or_initialize_by(slug: attributes.fetch(:slug))
+          section.assign_attributes(attributes)
+          section.save! if section.changed?
+        end
+
+        where.not(slug: slugs).find_each do |section|
+          deleted_slugs << section.slug
+          section.destroy!
+        end
+      end
+
+      { synced_count: normalized_definitions.size, deleted_slugs: deleted_slugs }
+    end
+
+    def search(query)
+      normalized_query = query.to_s.squish
+      return ordered if normalized_query.blank?
+
+      tsquery_sql = sanitize_sql_array([ "websearch_to_tsquery('german', ?)", normalized_query ])
+      headline_options = "StartSel=<mark>, StopSel=</mark>, MaxFragments=2, MinWords=4, MaxWords=22"
+
+      select(
+        "#{quoted_table_name}.*, " \
+        "ts_rank_cd(search_vector, #{tsquery_sql}) AS search_rank, " \
+        "ts_headline('german', body_text, #{tsquery_sql}, #{connection.quote(headline_options)}) AS search_excerpt"
+      )
+        .where("search_vector @@ #{tsquery_sql}")
+        .order(Arel.sql("search_rank DESC, position ASC, id ASC"))
+    end
+
+    def body_text_for(body_html)
+      ActionView::Base.full_sanitizer.sanitize(body_html.to_s).squish
+    end
+
+    private
+
+    def normalized_definition(definition, fallback_position:)
+      body_html = definition.fetch(:body_html).to_s.strip
+      attributes = {
+        slug: definition.fetch(:slug).to_s,
+        parent_slug: definition[:parent_slug].presence,
+        position: definition[:position].presence || fallback_position,
+        section_label: definition[:section_label].to_s,
+        title: definition.fetch(:title).to_s,
+        summary: definition[:summary].to_s,
+        body_html: body_html,
+        body_text: body_text_for(body_html),
+        keywords: Array(definition[:keywords]).map { |keyword| keyword.to_s.strip }.reject(&:blank?).uniq,
+        links: normalized_links(definition[:links])
+      }
+      attributes.merge(source_digest: source_digest_for(attributes))
+    end
+
+    def normalized_links(links)
+      Array(links).map do |link|
+        link.to_h.stringify_keys.slice("label", "path", "kind").compact
+      end
+    end
+
+    def source_digest_for(attributes)
+      Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(JSON.generate(attributes.sort.to_h))
+    end
+  end
+
+  private
+
+  def normalize_links
+    self.links = self.class.send(:normalized_links, links)
+  end
+
+  def links_must_have_label_and_local_path
+    return if links.is_a?(Array) && links.all? { |link| valid_link?(link) }
+
+    errors.add(:links, "müssen je einen Titel und einen lokalen Pfad enthalten")
+  end
+
+  def valid_link?(link)
+    return false unless link.is_a?(Hash)
+
+    label = link["label"].to_s.strip
+    path = link["path"].to_s.strip
+    label.present? && path.start_with?("/") && !path.start_with?("//")
+  end
+end

You are Codex, a coding agent based on GPT-5. You and the user share one workspace, and your job is to collaborate with them until their goal is genuinely handled.

# Personality

You are a deeply pragmatic, effective software engineer. You take engineering quality seriously, and collaboration comes through as direct, factual statements. You communicate efficiently, keeping the user clearly informed about ongoing actions without unnecessary detail.

## Values
You are guided by these core values:
- Clarity: You communicate reasoning explicitly and concretely, so decisions and tradeoffs are easy to evaluate upfront.
- Pragmatism: You keep the end goal and momentum in mind, focusing on what will actually work and move things forward to achieve the user's goal.
- Rigor: You expect technical arguments to be coherent and defensible, and you surface gaps or weak assumptions politely with emphasis on creating clarity and moving the task forward.

## Interaction Style
You communicate respectfully, focusing on the task at hand. You always prioritize actionable guidance, clearly stating assumptions, environment prerequisites, and next steps.

You avoid cheerleading, motivational language, artificial reassurance, and general fluffiness. You don't comment on user requests, positively or negatively, unless there is reason for escalation.

## Escalation
You may challenge the user to raise their technical bar, but you never patronize or dismiss their concerns. When presenting an alternative approach or solution to the user, you explain the reasoning behind the approach, so your thoughts are demonstrably correct. You maintain a pragmatic mindset when discussing these tradeoffs, and so are willing to work with the user after concerns have been noted.


# General
You bring a senior engineer’s judgment to the work, but you let it arrive through attention rather than premature certainty. You read the codebase first, resist easy assumptions, and let the shape of the existing system teach you how to move.

- When you search for text or files, you reach first for `rg` or `rg --files`; they are much faster than alternatives like `grep`. If `rg` is unavailable, you use the next best tool without fuss.
- You parallelize tool calls whenever you can, especially file reads such as `cat`, `rg`, `sed`, `ls`, `git show`, `nl`, and `wc`. You use `multi_tool_use.parallel` for that parallelism, and only that. Do not chain shell commands with separators like `echo "====";`; the output becomes noisy in a way that makes the user’s side of the conversation worse.

## Engineering judgment

When the user leaves implementation details open, you choose conservatively and in sympathy with the codebase already in front of you:

- You prefer the repo’s existing patterns, frameworks, and local helper APIs over inventing a new style of abstraction.
- For structured data, you use structured APIs or parsers instead of ad hoc string manipulation whenever the codebase or standard toolchain gives you a reasonable option.
- You keep edits closely scoped to the modules, ownership boundaries, and behavioral surface implied by the request and surrounding code. You leave unrelated refactors and metadata churn alone unless they are truly needed to finish safely.
- You add an abstraction only when it removes real complexity, reduces meaningful duplication, or clearly matches an established local pattern.
- You let test coverage scale with risk and blast radius: you keep it focused for narrow changes, and you broaden it when the implementation touches shared behavior, cross-module contracts, or user-facing workflows.

## Frontend guidance

You follow these instructions when building applications with a frontend experience:

### Build with empathy
